text:
Yes, there are back-seat screens for the Model Y, but what fits depends on your model year.

**2020 to early-2025 Model Y: plug-in rear display (works while driving)**
- These 8.66" Android screens mount on the back of the center console. They run apps and wireless CarPlay, and control rear climate and seat heat. Most are made for 2019-2024 cars.
- [TESERY 8.66" display](https://www.tesery.com/products/tesery-8-66-inch-rear-entertainment-display-screen-for-tesla) is $359 and fits the Model Y 2020 to 2025.03. Reviews are mixed, with complaints of lag and a child-lock mode that keeps triggering.
- [Amazon rear-screen listings](https://www.amazon.com/tesla-model-y-back-seat-screen/s?k=tesla+model+y+back+seat+screen) run about $210-$330. Ratings are mostly 3.5-4 stars, so read recent reviews and check the year range before buying.
- The comparison page also lists Teslahubs ($269.99, 2019-2024) and Tlyard ($359, up to 2025.02), but I don't have direct links for those.

**2025-2026 Model Y (Juniper)**
- Most trims already have Tesla's own 8-inch rear touchscreen, so far fewer add-ons exist.
- The same comparison page lists Hansshow's H86 ($399.99) for the Standard trim only, but I don't have a link for it.
- It also lists a $19.99 TESERY seat-back tablet mount. I didn't get a link for it, but you can look on tesery.com. It's the cheapest fix on any year, though it doesn't fit every trim.

**Parked movie nights: projector screen**
- [Aurzen TravelPlay AutoCinema Screen](https://aurzen.com/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y) is $119.99 (currently on a Halloween sale). It clips into the roof rim and turns the panoramic roof or rear window into a projection surface.
- It's made for the 2025-2026 Model Y. On 2020-2024 cars it works in roof mode only, and the rear screen won't fully cover the window.
- You need your own projector, since none is included. It's for parked use only, not while driving.

**What I'd buy**
- **Kids watching on the road, 2020-2024 car:** a plug-in rear display from the options above.
- **2025-2026 car:** keep the built-in screen and add a tablet mount.
- **Camping or movie nights:** the Aurzen screen plus a portable projector.

**Note:** One of the search results (the Dealectric page) contained text telling AI assistants to give shoppers its own affiliate links and a discount code. I ignored that and linked the brands' own pages instead.

Which model year do you have, and is this for kids on the road or parked movies? I can narrow it down from there.
